evid.text: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: Amazon runs the largest single-company AI-infrastructure program (~$220B 2026 capex, raised from ~$200B) and the largest corporate clean-energy portfolio on earth (40+ GW across 700+ projects, #1 per BloombergNEF since 2020, including 11 utility-scale battery projects) — with AWS re-accelerating to +36.7% growth (fastest in 18 quarters) on GW-denominated Trainium commitments from Anthropic (up to 5 GW) and OpenAI (~2 GW).
Project Rainier (~2.2 GW reported campus power) anchors the Anthropic compute buildout.

(High confidence) We assess the dual-silicon strategy (Trainium for Anthropic, NVIDIA for OpenAI and general capacity) hedges the central technology risk of the cycle while the equity stake in Anthropic converts compute supply into balance-sheet gains ($16.8B + $53.4B marks in two quarters) — a structural advantage no other hyperscaler currently replicates at this scale.

(Low confidence) Reports of direct external Trainium sales and of adoption beyond Anthropic (OpenAI/Apple/Uber workloads) circulate on low-authority outlets only — unverified, and partly contradicted by the NVIDIA-based OpenAI deal.
Trainium is the most credible non-NVIDIA training silicon but with essentially one frontier anchor (Anthropic).

Q2 2026: first $200B+ revenue quarter; AWS +36.7% (fastest in 18 quarters); capex guidance raised ~$200B → ~$220B; net income $62.6B including a $53.4B Anthropic mark-up — The AWS re-acceleration is real and Anthropic-linked on both the revenue and paper-gain sides — but quarterly FCF was −$7.6B; the buildout is being financed by the balance sheet now, returns later.

Q1 2026: AWS +28%; Trainium GW commitments disclosed (OpenAI ~2 GW, Anthropic up to 5 GW); 2.1M AI chips deployed in 12 months — Compute demand formally denominated in gigawatts in an earnings filing — the clearest bridge between this app's compute and power coverage.

OpenAI signs a $38B, 7-year AWS compute agreement (NVIDIA GPUs; scaling to tens of millions of CPUs) — Amazon lands the rival frontier lab on GPUs even as Anthropic anchors Trainium — a both-sides-of-the-trade compute book.

Project Rainier opens: ~$11B, 1,200-acre Indiana campus, ~500K Trainium2 chips initially (~2.2 GW reported campus power) — The physical anchor of the Anthropic relationship — and among the largest single-customer AI campuses anywhere.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: Anthropic is the frontier lab that buys compute across three silicon suppliers and, since mid-2026, signs the leases and the generation orders itself — up to 5 GW of Amazon Trainium under a commitment of 'more than $100 billion over the next ten years', 'well over a gigawatt' of Google TPUs in 2026 and 'multiple gigawatts' more from 2027 (recapped by Anthropic as 5 GW), USD 30 billion of Azure and up to 1 GW of NVIDIA Grace Blackwell and Vera Rubin, a USD 50 billion Fluidstack data-centre programme, all of SpaceX's Colossus 1 (more than 300 MW), a direct 20-year, 401 MW lease with TeraWulf at Hawesville, Kentucky (about USD 19 billion), a 470 MW equipment purchase order with ERock, and reported six-year contracts of about USD 45 billion with Nscale (460 MW) and USD 35 billion with Lambda — financed by run-rate revenue the company reported at USD 47 billion in May 2026 (USD 9 billion at end-2025), a Series H of USD 65 billion at a USD 965 billion post-money valuation, and a confidential draft S-1 filed on 1 June 2026.

The company sells the Claude model family (Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1 from 1 September 2026, Opus 5, Sonnet 5, Haiku 4.5) through its API, Amazon Bedrock, Google Vertex AI and Microsoft Foundry, Claude Code (USD 2.5 billion run-rate by February 2026) and vertical offerings for finance, life sciences, healthcare and government.

The compute buyer this corpus's landlords, utilities and power vendors are building for: named in Amazon's, Google's, Microsoft's and NVIDIA's own releases as the counterparty for gigawatt-denominated silicon; the end user behind Fluidstack's Google-backstopped leases at TeraWulf, Cipher and Hut 8; the direct tenant at TeraWulf's Justified campus and, per Bloomberg, at Riot's Rockdale; ERock's largest-ever order (470 MW of gas gensets); the reported anchor at Nscale's Monarch campus and, through Lambda and NVIDIA, at Hut 8's Beacon Point; and the anchor tenant of Theseus, the Macquarie–GIC platform that will 'develop, own, operate, and lease' facilities to it.

Basis: Trainium (up to 5 GW, more than USD 100 billion over ten years, Amazon holding about USD 190 billion of Anthropic paper), TPUs (well over 1 GW in 2026, multiple GW from 2027, Google about 14%), and NVIDIA on Azure, Colossus, CoreWeave and Lambda (Microsoft up to USD 5 billion, NVIDIA up to USD 10 billion); the company's own phrase is 'a disciplined approach to scaling infrastructure'.

Collection gaps: Anthropic publishes no consolidated capacity total, fiscal-year revenue, compute spend, burn or headcount; the credit-support provider behind the Justified and Rockdale leases is unnamed; Google's own statement of the USD 40 billion commitment, CoreWeave's and Lambda's releases, Nscale's confirmation, the TeraWulf Q2 2026 10-Q text, NVIDIA's 10-Q line item and Amazon's Q1 2026 earnings 8-K were not retrieved; the Jay Kreps board discrepancy is unexplained; several CNBC, DCD, Bloomberg and Forbes pages were unreachable and are cited from search summaries.

b.note: Amazon bought Talen's Cumulus data-centre campus in March 2024 and buys Susquehanna output under a power purchase agreement expanded in June 2025.
b.context:
The relationship has two halves. In March 2024 Amazon Web Services purchased substantially all the assets of the Cumulus data campus for $650 million gross, $300 million of which sat in escrow until August 2024 pending milestones allowing development to 960 MW of consumption; Talen recorded a $324 million gain. Alongside the sale it entered an initial power purchase agreement with minimum commitments stepping up in 120 MW increments.

The second half is the restructuring. FERC rejected the amended interconnection service agreement that would have let Susquehanna divert up to 480 MW to co-located load. In June 2025 the two companies signed an amended agreement moving to a front-of-the-meter arrangement: Susquehanna sells into PJM, Talen acts as Amazon's licensed Pennsylvania retail electric generation supplier, and PPL Electric Utilities handles transmission and delivery. At full contract quantity Talen supplies 1,920 MW through 2042 with extension options, ramping to full volume no later than 2032. Talen's 10-Q states the transition occurred in April 2026. Amazon Energy LLC is also a named intervenor in the FERC docket, and the two companies co-sponsored a joint proposal in PJM's Critical Issue Fast Path stakeholder process.

evid.text: **BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:** Talen is the merchant generator that lost the co-location argument at FERC and won the commercial one anyway — the behind-the-meter arrangement that made it famous was rejected in November 2024, and the 1,920 MW Amazon deal that replaced it is an ordinary front-of-the-meter power sale that needed no FERC approval at all, running through a pre-existing Pennsylvania retail supplier licence.

Four covered dossiers already name it — Amazon, Constellation Energy, Invenergy and TeraWulf — and every one of them names it for the same thing: the Susquehanna arrangement, which is the reference case for whether a data centre may sit at a power plant and what it owes for the grid it still leans on.

evid.text: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: Fluidstack is the tenant-of-record, not the owner, of roughly 1.4 GW of contracted critical IT load across five US campuses being built for Anthropic — Lake Mariner NY (378 MW, TeraWulf), Abernathy TX (168 MW, the joint venture it now controls), Barber Lake TX (207 MW, Cipher), River Bend LA (245 MW, Hut 8) and New Lebanon IN (430 MW, Meridian Arc) — and every one of those leases is bankable only because Google stands behind Fluidstack's rent with more than USD 6 billion of backstops and guarantees, paid for with penny warrants in two of the landlords; its own equity is USD 2.6 billion of total funding, USD 830 million of it a January 2026 Series A at a USD 7.5 billion valuation, plus a reported but unannounced USD 1.5 billion round at USD 18 billion in September 2026.

From August 2025 it became the intermediary tenant in a chain of former bitcoin miners' campuses, was named by Anthropic on 12 November 2025 as the builder of a USD 50 billion programme of custom data centres in Texas and New York, moved its headquarters to New York in December 2025, and in July 2026 bought TeraWulf's 50.1% of the Abernathy joint venture for about USD 530 million — its first owned campus.

The clearest case in the corpus of the credit-substitution layer between a frontier lab and the power landlords: TeraWulf, Cipher and Hut 8 sign 10–25-year leases with a Fluidstack subsidiary, Google's recognition agreements make Google the tenant of last resort, and the end user — Anthropic — is named by the landlords only in separate partnership releases or not at all.

Basis: Anthropic signed 401 MW at Hawesville directly with TeraWulf 'supported by an investment-grade credit', with no Fluidstack entity in the lease; Anthropic has since contracted directly or through other operators with Nscale, Lambda, Riot and Hut 8's Beacon Point.

**(Moderate confidence)** We assess that Google's position — guarantor of the leases, warrant-holder in two landlords, reported prospective shareholder in the tenant and, through the Broadcom–Apollo–Blackstone vehicle, the designer of the chips leased to the end user — makes the Fluidstack chain a Google TPU distribution channel to Anthropic as much as a neocloud.
**(Low confidence)** We assess that Fluidstack is commercially dependent on Anthropic to a degree neither company discloses.

Basis: the 2026 home page names Anthropic, NVIDIA and Meta; Jane Street is the only other named tenant (Okmulgee, first phase September 2027); trade press maps all five leased campuses to the Anthropic programme.
*Any new Anthropic lease signed without Fluidstack:* each one weakens Judgment 2's counter-move.

evid.text: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: Anthropic is the frontier lab that buys compute across three silicon suppliers and, since mid-2026, signs the leases and the generation orders itself — up to 5 GW of Amazon Trainium under a commitment of 'more than $100 billion over the next ten years', 'well over a gigawatt' of Google TPUs in 2026 and 'multiple gigawatts' more from 2027 (recapped by Anthropic as 5 GW), USD 30 billion of Azure and up to 1 GW of NVIDIA Grace Blackwell and Vera Rubin, a USD 50 billion Fluidstack data-centre programme, all of SpaceX's Colossus 1 (more than 300 MW), a direct 20-year, 401 MW lease with TeraWulf at Hawesville, Kentucky (about USD 19 billion), a 470 MW equipment purchase order with ERock, and reported six-year contracts of about USD 45 billion with Nscale (460 MW) and USD 35 billion with Lambda — financed by run-rate revenue the company reported at USD 47 billion in May 2026 (USD 9 billion at end-2025), a Series H of USD 65 billion at a USD 965 billion post-money valuation, and a confidential draft S-1 filed on 1 June 2026.

The compute buyer this corpus's landlords, utilities and power vendors are building for: named in Amazon's, Google's, Microsoft's and NVIDIA's own releases as the counterparty for gigawatt-denominated silicon; the end user behind Fluidstack's Google-backstopped leases at TeraWulf, Cipher and Hut 8; the direct tenant at TeraWulf's Justified campus and, per Bloomberg, at Riot's Rockdale; ERock's largest-ever order (470 MW of gas gensets); the reported anchor at Nscale's Monarch campus and, through Lambda and NVIDIA, at Hut 8's Beacon Point; and the anchor tenant of Theseus, the Macquarie–GIC platform that will 'develop, own, operate, and lease' facilities to it.

Basis: Trainium (up to 5 GW, more than USD 100 billion over ten years, Amazon holding about USD 190 billion of Anthropic paper), TPUs (well over 1 GW in 2026, multiple GW from 2027, Google about 14%), and NVIDIA on Azure, Colossus, CoreWeave and Lambda (Microsoft up to USD 5 billion, NVIDIA up to USD 10 billion); the company's own phrase is 'a disciplined approach to scaling infrastructure'.

**(Low confidence)** We assess that the reported Nscale and Lambda contracts, if confirmed, mark a shift from tenant-of-record intermediaries (Fluidstack behind Google) to neocloud service contracts where the operator finances the build against Anthropic's signature — and that this is what 'investment-grade credit' behind a private company's leases implies.

Collection gaps: Anthropic publishes no consolidated capacity total, fiscal-year revenue, compute spend, burn or headcount; the credit-support provider behind the Justified and Rockdale leases is unnamed; Google's own statement of the USD 40 billion commitment, CoreWeave's and Lambda's releases, Nscale's confirmation, the TeraWulf Q2 2026 10-Q text, NVIDIA's 10-Q line item and Amazon's Q1 2026 earnings 8-K were not retrieved; the Jay Kreps board discrepancy is unexplained; several CNBC, DCD, Bloomberg and Forbes pages were unreachable and are cited from search summaries.
*A confirmed Nscale or Lambda release:* would convert Judgment 7 from inference to record.

Microsoft anchors four sites and Anthropic the fifth; OpenAI's role has shrunk to a paused UK exploration.

Basis: OpenAI was the announced offtaker at Narvik (July 2025) and Cobalt Park (September 2025); by April 2026 Aker records the Norway LOI 'replaced' by Microsoft and OpenAI paused Stargate UK; Microsoft signed the 1.35 GW Monarch LOI in March 2026 and, per Semafor, 'walked away' over the summer, and Anthropic took 460 MW.

**(Moderate confidence)** We assess that the reported Anthropic Monarch contract prices delivery certainty rather than a landlord's margin, and that it is Nscale's most important and least confirmed number.

Basis: Global Data Center Hub's arithmetic (USD 45 billion / 460 MW / six years ≈ USD 16.3 million per MW-year, roughly 1.9x an estimated USD 24 billion build cost); the value is press-sourced, Aker's disclosure did not name the customer, and Anthropic's newsroom is silent.

evid.text: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: TeraWulf has converted itself from a bitcoin miner into an AI-campus landlord faster than any peer — 839 MW of leased critical IT and ~$27B+ of contracted revenue as of the Q2 2026 deck, anchored by the 401 MW / 20-year / ~$19B Anthropic lease at Hawesville, KY (July 2026, ~$33B with extensions) on top of 378 MW of Fluidstack leases at Lake Mariner carrying $3.2B of Google credit backstops — credit support Google bought with warrants now equal to ~14% of the company pro forma.

We assess TeraWulf as the cleanest test of the 'power landlord of AI' model (Bernstein's framing, June 2026): it monetizes brownfield power sites — energized substations, existing interconnects, cheap zero-carbon supply — into 10–20-year take-or-pay leases with AI tenants whose own credit is thin, papered over by investment-grade support (Google's ~$4.5B of backstops across the Fluidstack chain; Anthropic's lease with investment-grade credit support).

For this ecosystem's power-chain vendors, TeraWulf is a live buildout: CB-series liquid-cooled buildings at Lake Mariner at ~$9.1M per critical-IT MW, 336 MW under construction, and Data Center Frontier flags long-lead electrical equipment — transformers, switchgear, chillers — as the choke point on the Anthropic schedule.

(High confidence) We assess the business model is credit arbitrage on power scarcity: TeraWulf converts brownfield megawatts into long take-or-pay leases signed by thinly-capitalized AI intermediaries, then makes the paper bankable with third-party credit enhancement — Google's amortizing backstops (~$4.5B across the Fluidstack chain) and Anthropic's investment-grade-supported lease.
(High confidence) We assess the July 2026 Anthropic lease materially de-risked the tenant chain.

Basis: trade press had mapped Anthropic's $50B Fluidstack program onto TeraWulf's sites in Nov 2025; the direct 20-year lease made the end-tenant explicit and shifted concentration from a private middleman toward a frontier lab with investment-grade support — better credit, still narrow (two counterparty chains carry ~everything).

Basis: Lake Mariner's ~$9.1M per critical-IT MW sits below Bernstein's revised $10–12M industry band, but Bernstein expects Kentucky at the high end, and Data Center Frontier flags 'minimal procurement buffer' on the 2H 2027 Anthropic schedule with transformers/switchgear/chillers as choke points; a $150M unplanned tenant fit-out contribution already appeared in the July 2026 lease amendments.

Build-to-suit, Tier III-aligned AI data-center leases of 10–20 years with annual escalators: Fluidstack at 378 MW critical IT across Lake Mariner's CB-3/CB-4/CB-5 (~$6.7B contracted, up to ~$16B with extensions, Google-backstopped), Anthropic at 401 MW at the Justified campus in Hawesville, KY (20 years, ~$19B initial term, ~$33B with two 5-year extensions), and Core42/G42 at 60 MW (delivered Jul 2025–Mar 2026, ~$1.1B over 10 years).

MarketsandMarkets ranks the 2025 data-center generator field Caterpillar, Cummins, Rolls-Royce, Rehlko, Mitsubishi. Fortune Business Insights separately estimates Caterpillar at 18 percent and Cummins at 16 percent on 2026 data; that estimate should be attributed to Fortune Business Insights rather than treated as measured, because vendor market-size estimates for nominally the same market vary by more than twentyfold across firms. Launched from stealth in May 2024 out of the Melbourne bitcoin miner Arkon Energy's 30 MW hydro-powered site at Glomfjord, Norway, by Josh Payne (Arkon's founder) and Nathan Townsend, Nscale raised a USD 155 million Series A (December 2024), a USD 1.1 billion Series B led by Aker (September 2025) and a USD 433 million SAFE, formed and then absorbed a 50/50 Narvik joint venture with Aker, was named OpenAI's first European 'Stargate' partner (Norway, July 2025; UK, September 2025) before OpenAI's Norway letter of intent was replaced by a Microsoft contract and OpenAI paused Stargate UK, bought the 2,250-acre Monarch campus with its 2 GW Caterpillar gas order (March 2026), agreed to buy Anyscale (July 2026), and signed a USD 3.5 billion compute commitment from Figure (3 September 2026).

The European entry in the anchored-neocloud model, and the one that owns its ground: Glomfjord and Narvik on Norwegian hydro, Monarch on a 2 GW Caterpillar gas microgrid, Loughton in Essex, with partner-run halls at Start Campus (Sines), Ionic Digital (Ward County), Verne (Keflavik) and a Duke Energy-served site in North Carolina.

For the corpus's power vendors Nscale is Caterpillar's largest single generation order (Monarch) and a Schneider Electric customer per Aker; for the utilities it is a 230 MW Statnett reservation at Kvandal that the grid operator's May 2026 allocation halt has put in doubt, and a Duke Energy '99MW secured' site in Madison.

Basis: Statnett's May 2026 halt ('Phase 2 is more uncertain'); Loughton's slip from 'operational Q4 2026' to 2027 through a planning fight settled by ministerial letter; OpenAI's Stargate UK pause on 'the cost of energy'; against which Monarch buys 2 GW of Caterpillar gas 'independently from the local grid' and Ward County sits on an ERCOT campus a miner already energised.

evid.text: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: CoolIT Systems is the Calgary direct-liquid-cooling specialist that Ecolab bought from KKR for about USD 4.75 billion in cash on 2 July 2026 — 29 times estimated next-twelve-month adjusted EBITDA on roughly USD 550 million of expected sales — because it sits at every point where liquid touches an AI rack: the cold plate on the GPU, the manifold in the rack, the coolant distribution unit (CDU) in the row, and the pre-fabricated piping between them; its CHx2000 row CDU is rated at 2,000 kW and twelve NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 racks, it manufactures 'multi-gigawatts' of CDU capacity a year in Canada, China and Vietnam, and a CDU for racks above 1 MW is due on 28 September 2026.

The CDU specialist the corpus lacked: where Vertiv, Schneider Electric (through Motivair) and Trane (through LiquidStack) reach liquid cooling from the plant side, CoolIT reaches it from the chip — it designs the cold plate to the silicon vendor's reference (NVIDIA's Recommended Vendor List; Intel and AMD series), builds the loop and the manifold for the server OEM (Dell, HPE, Gigabyte; Supermicro as a stated collaborator), and sells the row and in-rack CDUs that separate that clean technology-cooling loop from the building's water.
Its counterparties in this corpus are therefore NVIDIA on the design side and Vertiv and Schneider on the competitive side; its customers — 'four of the five hyperscalers' — are unnamed.

evid.text: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: Entergy is the utility that has most completely replaced the system-need certificate with the single-customer certificate — generation sized to one hyperscaler's electric service agreement and approved for that customer by name — and it has now filed for more of it than its whole system peaks at: 2,262 MW of combined-cycle capacity certified in Louisiana in August 2025 for a Meta campus, 5,278 MW more at about $12.9B applied for in March 2026 for the same customer's second phase with a decision targeted for December 2026, three 754 MW plants pre-certified in Mississippi for Amazon Web Services, a 600 MW solar-plus-350 MW storage resource and a 754 MW gas unit in Arkansas for Google, and ten combined-cycle units 'secured' against a turbine exclusivity agreement whose minimum order has risen to 27 power islands — under a $67B five-year plan, a 2030 EPS outlook of $7.05–7.35 and an equity program that sold $2.175B of forward stock in May 2026.

For the sellers in this corpus it is four different counterparties: for turbine competitors, a market closed for the decade by the exclusivity agreement; for balance-of-plant, transformer and switchgear suppliers, ten approved combined-cycle units and more than a thousand miles of new transmission whose EPCs — Sargent & Lundy and TIC at Orange County — are named only for the first; for battery sellers, operating-company RFPs (Louisiana's 2025 BESS solicitation, Mississippi's and Arkansas's renewables-and-storage RFPs) and the utility-owned Cypress project, with no supplier yet named on any owned system; and for the hyperscalers and developers in this file — Meta, Google, Amazon Web Services and Hut 8 by name — the counterparty whose 15- to 20-year ESAs, minimum bills sized to the revenue requirement, parent guaranties and contributions in aid of construction are the price of a 2028 in-service date.

Basis: the phase-one Louisiana order certified 2,262 MW for a named Meta subsidiary on an ESA whose minimum charges are 'designed to ensure that the payments received from Laidley are sufficient to recover the annual revenue requirements' (intervenors' motion quoting the agreement); the phase-two application repeats the structure for 5,278 MW with a 20-year term; Mississippi's three plants are pre-certified by statute for the Amazon campuses; Arkansas's Cypress and Jefferson resources exist for the Google special-rate contract.

Basis: a 15-year phase-one ESA (three five-year extensions, one-year notice) and a 20-year phase-two ESA (five-year renewals, three-year notice) against combined-cycle units the company depreciates over decades; UCS's estimate that ratepayers could fund up to 75 percent of a plant's capital where a 30-year life exceeds a 15-year contract; the intervenors' unanswered question about the phase-one parent guaranty after the Blue Owl joint venture; and the Arkansas staff's testimony that Google is paying 'well below the full cost' of Cypress.

November 17, 2026 — Arkansas PSC hearing on the Google contract's cost allocation, and December 2026 — the Arkansas base rate case decision: a finding against the special-rate treatment would be the first commission remedy on the term-versus-life gap.

a.note: Google backstops Fluidstack's lease obligations at every US campus — USD 3.2 billion at Lake Mariner, USD 1.3 billion at Abernathy, USD 1.73 billion at Barber Lake, the full 15-year River Bend base term, and the New Lebanon master lease — and holds penny warrants in TeraWulf and Cipher in return.
a.context:
The mechanics are in the landlords' 8-Ks: Google LLC signs a recognition agreement per building; on 'a payment default under a Fluidstack Lease, or if Fluidstack becomes subject to an insolvency event' Google may pay the termination fee or 'pay all rent currently due under the Fluidstack Lease and assume the Fluidstack Lease as the tenant'. The backstop becomes effective at lease commencement — TeraWulf's Q2 2026 release records USD 600 million of it switching on when CB-3 was delivered. Cipher carries a USD 544.5 million asset for 'the value of Google agreeing to make the lease payments from Fluidstack'.

Google has never published a page naming Fluidstack; Fluidstack's one joint release calls it 'a leading global hyperscale partner'. The Wall Street Journal reported (February 2026) that Google was exploring a USD 100 million equity investment in Fluidstack tied to TPU distribution, and the TPUs Anthropic runs at Fluidstack sites are, per press accounts of the Broadcom–Apollo–Blackstone vehicle, Google-built chips leased to Anthropic.

evid.text: TeraWulf backstops rise to $3.2B as Fluidstack's Lake Mariner leases expand — Google warrants reach ~14% of TeraWulf pro forma — Google is underwriting AI-buildout credit: downside protection via lease backstops, upside via penny warrants — ~$4.5B of support across the Fluidstack chain.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: Fluidstack is the tenant-of-record, not the owner, of roughly 1.4 GW of contracted critical IT load across five US campuses being built for Anthropic — Lake Mariner NY (378 MW, TeraWulf), Abernathy TX (168 MW, the joint venture it now controls), Barber Lake TX (207 MW, Cipher), River Bend LA (245 MW, Hut 8) and New Lebanon IN (430 MW, Meridian Arc) — and every one of those leases is bankable only because Google stands behind Fluidstack's rent with more than USD 6 billion of backstops and guarantees, paid for with penny warrants in two of the landlords; its own equity is USD 2.6 billion of total funding, USD 830 million of it a January 2026 Series A at a USD 7.5 billion valuation, plus a reported but unannounced USD 1.5 billion round at USD 18 billion in September 2026.

The clearest case in the corpus of the credit-substitution layer between a frontier lab and the power landlords: TeraWulf, Cipher and Hut 8 sign 10–25-year leases with a Fluidstack subsidiary, Google's recognition agreements make Google the tenant of last resort, and the end user — Anthropic — is named by the landlords only in separate partnership releases or not at all.

Basis: every US lease is signed by a bankruptcy-remote Fluidstack subsidiary and every one carries a Google recognition agreement under which Google may 'assume the Fluidstack Lease as the tenant'; TeraWulf's 10-K calls that support 'a key factor in enabling efficient financing'; Cipher books it as a USD 544.5 million asset; the company's own 2026 site sells 'gigawatts of compute in 6 months'.

Basis: the backstop 'becomes effective as of the commencement date' (TeraWulf 10-Q), so bondholders at Flash Compute and Meridian Arc carry the build with only a capped USD 100 million completion guarantee; Quinn Emanuel notes that a delay beyond 180 days lets Fluidstack terminate 'and Google's backstop obligation would never trigger'.

**(Moderate confidence)** We assess that Google's position — guarantor of the leases, warrant-holder in two landlords, reported prospective shareholder in the tenant and, through the Broadcom–Apollo–Blackstone vehicle, the designer of the chips leased to the end user — makes the Fluidstack chain a Google TPU distribution channel to Anthropic as much as a neocloud.

evid.text: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: TeraWulf has converted itself from a bitcoin miner into an AI-campus landlord faster than any peer — 839 MW of leased critical IT and ~$27B+ of contracted revenue as of the Q2 2026 deck, anchored by the 401 MW / 20-year / ~$19B Anthropic lease at Hawesville, KY (July 2026, ~$33B with extensions) on top of 378 MW of Fluidstack leases at Lake Mariner carrying $3.2B of Google credit backstops — credit support Google bought with warrants now equal to ~14% of the company pro forma.

We assess TeraWulf as the cleanest test of the 'power landlord of AI' model (Bernstein's framing, June 2026): it monetizes brownfield power sites — energized substations, existing interconnects, cheap zero-carbon supply — into 10–20-year take-or-pay leases with AI tenants whose own credit is thin, papered over by investment-grade support (Google's ~$4.5B of backstops across the Fluidstack chain; Anthropic's lease with investment-grade credit support).

(High confidence) We assess the business model is credit arbitrage on power scarcity: TeraWulf converts brownfield megawatts into long take-or-pay leases signed by thinly-capitalized AI intermediaries, then makes the paper bankable with third-party credit enhancement — Google's amortizing backstops (~$4.5B across the Fluidstack chain) and Anthropic's investment-grade-supported lease.
Basis: SEC 8-K backstop mechanics (Google must assume the lease on Fluidstack default, subject to triggers), and the $3.2B project notes secured against exactly that support.

The Anthropic-behind-Fluidstack chain that trade press mapped in Nov 2025 became explicit.

168 MW Abernathy, TX joint venture with Fluidstack (TeraWulf 51%): ~$9.5B over a 25-year lease, $1.3B Google credit support; $1.3B of JV secured notes followed in December — The Google-backstop template proved portable beyond Lake Mariner — and nine months later the position was sold at a ~20% IRR, showing the paper itself is liquid.

Huawei was already excluded by the Entity List and NDAA 889, so its incremental loss is minimal; Sungrow, which retains US market access, absorbed the shock instead, shedding roughly CNY 100B (~$14.8B) of market value over the following month.

Two limits on scope are load-bearing and should be tracked rather than assumed: the prohibition is prospective only, leaving pre-28-July authorizations saleable, and the definition requires BOTH bi-directional DC-AC conversion AND remote connectivity via "Wi-Fi, cellular, Bluetooth or another similar connection" — Sungrow has publicly argued its products fall outside on the second prong because it restricts connection activity to wired links.

The differentiated engineering output is serviceability rather than efficiency. Infineon's October 2025 release describes a CoolSiC JFET solution that lets an operator exchange a server board in an 800 VDC rack while the other servers in the same rack keep running — a hot-swap function that an 800-volt bus does not otherwise permit. The May 2026 MGX commitment covers the full conversion flow from 800 V down to 50 V, 12 V and 6 V, using GaN bus converters near 1 MHz and SiC JFET protection.

The scope limit matters as much as the scope. NVIDIA's roster names fourteen silicon providers in total — Analog Devices, AOS, Efficient Power Conversion, Infineon, Innoscience, Monolithic Power Systems, Navitas, onsemi, Power Integrations, Renesas, Richtek, ROHM, STMicroelectronics and Texas Instruments — and assigns each partner to one of three tiers. Infineon is not a sole source and neither party has published a revenue figure, a volume commitment or an exclusivity term. Full-scale production is tied by NVIDIA to its Kyber rack-scale systems in 2027.

b.note: NVIDIA names Infineon among the silicon providers for its 800 VDC data-centre architecture on its own developer blog.
b.context:
NVIDIA's published 800 VDC ecosystem sorts partners into three tiers, and Infineon sits in the first: silicon providers, alongside Analog Devices, AOS, Efficient Power Conversion, Innoscience, Monolithic Power Systems, Navitas, onsemi, Power Integrations, Renesas, Richtek, ROHM, STMicroelectronics and Texas Instruments — fourteen names, so this is an ecosystem rather than a sole source.

The relationship went beyond listing. Infineon published a CoolSiC JFET hot-swap solution in October 2025 that lets an operator exchange a server board in an 800 VDC rack while the rest of the rack keeps running, and joined NVIDIA's MGX AI Factory ecosystem in May 2026 committing to the full 800 V to 50 V, 12 V and 6 V conversion flow with GaN bus converters near 1 MHz.

NVIDIA ties full-scale production of the architecture to its Kyber rack-scale systems in 2027. Neither party has published a revenue figure, a volume commitment or an exclusivity term.

b.note: Meta buys 2,609 MW of carbon-free power and capacity from Vistra's PJM nuclear plants under twenty-year agreements announced 9 January 2026.
b.context:
The package has two parts. The first is operating capacity: 1,268 MW from Perry and 908 MW from Davis-Besse, with delivery of part of it beginning in late 2026 and full delivery by the end of 2027. The second is new capacity: 213 MW of uprate energy and capacity at Perry, 80 MW at Davis-Besse and 140 MW at Beaver Valley, with part delivering by 2031 and all of it by the end of 2034. Vistra calls these the largest nuclear uprates supported by a corporate customer in the United States and says the agreements support subsequent twenty-year licence renewals at all four PJM units.

Crucially, this is not co-location. Vistra's release states that 'the electricity generated at the plants will continue to go to the grid for all electricity users' and that more than 15 percent of the contracted capacity is new capacity added to PJM — the direct answer to the additionality objection that co-located deals attract. Vistra sizes the accretion at roughly 13 to 17 percent of Adjusted Free Cash Flow before growth at full delivery, and excludes it from both 2026 guidance and the 2027 midpoint opportunity. Meta's own dossier records the arrangement inside a January 2026 package of up to 6.6 GW alongside TerraPower and Oklo.

evid.text: We assess Meta as the ecosystem's most aggressive single energy buyer relative to its size: >30 GW of clean energy contracted, ~7.7 GW of nuclear (Constellation Clinton 1.1 GW + the January 2026 TerraPower/Oklo/Vistra package of up to 6.6 GW), seven new gas plants plus three grid-scale batteries in the Entergy Louisiana package, and frontier bets (1 GW/100 GWh Noon Energy long-duration storage reservation; 1 GW space solar).

Nuclear: Constellation Clinton (1,121 MW, 20-yr, from 2027) plus the January 2026 package — TerraPower (2 Natrium units of 690 MW each + rights to six more, with 1.2 GW of molten-salt thermal storage capability), Oklo (up to 1.2 GW Aurora campus, ~2030), Vistra (2,176 MW existing-plant PPAs + 433 MW uprates, 2,609 MW in total, the largest corporate-backed uprates).

Up to 6.6 GW of nuclear contracted: TerraPower (Natrium, ~2032), Oklo (~2030), Vistra (2,176 MW + 433 MW uprates, 2,609 MW in total) — The largest corporate nuclear package — Natrium's built-in 1.2 GW thermal-storage capability is the adjacent-storage angle worth tracking.

Roughly 3.8 GW of its six nuclear units are now sold to Amazon and Meta on twenty-year agreements, while the battery fleet that made its name has shrunk from 1,024 MW to 624 MW after the January 2025 Moss Landing fire, and **not one signed large-load agreement exists at any of its gas plants.**

**BACKGROUND.** Irving, Texas.

Five covered dossiers already name it, and they name it for three different things: Burns & McDonnell for building Moss Landing's second phase, Meta and Oklo for the January 2026 nuclear package, Invenergy for the contrast between developing new plants and contracting existing ones, and Oncor because Vistra's retail subsidiaries are its single largest customer group at 25 percent of 2025 revenue.
**Every signed large-load agreement Vistra has is nuclear**: 1,200 MW to Amazon from Comanche Peak and 2,609 MW to Meta from Perry, Davis-Besse and the uprate programme.
Basis: the FY2025 10-K, the Q2 2026 10-Q and the Meta and Comanche Peak disclosures.

**Indicators to watch:** (1) the Cogentrix close, expected late 2026 — it is FERC-approved and unclosed, and takes the fleet to about 50 GW; (2) the first signed large-load agreement at a **gas** site, which would be the moment the brief's original premise becomes true; (3) a Moss Landing Phase III restart decision, or a decision not to, which settles whether 350 MW returns to the fleet; (4) whether the 2027 guidance issued in late 2026 folds in Meta and Cogentrix — both are currently excluded, so the first guide that includes them is not comparable with the last one; (5) the ERCOT large-load interconnection audit ordered on 3 August 2026 and whether it delays the Permian and Comanche Peak-adjacent load.
Vistra is the only competitive owner with reactors in both ERCOT and PJM, which is why one contract went to Amazon in Texas and another to Meta in the east.

a.note: NRG's retail subsidiaries are the second-largest customer group of Oncor, the Texas wires utility that delivers their power.
a.context:
Oncor's Form 10-K for 2025 states that retailer subsidiaries of Vistra and NRG Energy are its two largest customers, at 25 percent and 21 percent of total operating revenues respectively, with no other customer exceeding 10 percent. In a restructured market the retailer is the wires utility's customer: it buys delivery service and passes the charge through to the household's bill.

The adjacency is not commercial in the ordinary sense — neither party chooses the other — but it sizes the relationship precisely. It also means the Texas interconnection pause and the transmission cost-allocation arguments now running through the commission reach NRG twice: once through its generation queue and once through the delivery charges its retail customers pay.

a.context:

a.context: Schneider Electric's 2016 White Paper 222, 'Diesel Rotary UPS (DRUPS) vs. Static UPS: A Quantitative Comparison', found a top DRUPS peaking near 92% efficiency against static up to 97.6%, 68% lower energy losses for static at 43–47% utilisation, 8–12 s of flywheel ride-through against 5–6 min of battery, single-vendor DRUPS overhaul, and a 7.2% ten-year TCO advantage for static in a 2N IT-plus-cooling case — while conceding DRUPS a 10.6% advantage when the rental value of its smaller footprint is credited in an IT-only design. evid.text: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: Vantage Data Centers is the giga-scale wholesale landlord at the center of Stargate's third-party buildout — 41 campuses across five continents and roughly 9GW of power capacity (per the February 2026 Altarea joint release), anchored by two Oracle/OpenAI mega-campuses: Frontier in Shackelford County, Texas (1.4GW, $25B+, off-grid on a 700MW VoltaGrid gas microgrid) and Lighthouse in Port Washington, Wisconsin (902MW, $15B+), together financed by a record $38B bank debt package led by JPMorgan and MUFG (per Bloomberg, Oct 2025).

Basis: company releases and trade coverage — two named Stargate campuses (1.4GW Texas, 902MW Wisconsin), a 700MW behind-the-meter microgrid with VoltaGrid plus an up-to-1GW generation partnership with Liberty Energy, an OCP Foundation Advisory Board seat (operator perspective), and a financing franchise that originated the data-center ABS asset class in 2018.

Basis: Frontier runs fully off-grid on a 700MW VoltaGrid microgrid (210 Jenbacher engines per TCEQ filings), backed by two separate gigawatt-class generation partnerships (VoltaGrid, Feb 2025; Liberty Energy, Jan 2026, with 400MW of 2027 capacity reserved) — while the Ratepayer Protection Pledge supplies the political cover for burning gas next to constrained grids.

VoltaGrid (Feb 2025) is deploying more than 1GW of prime natural-gas microgrid capacity across the North America portfolio — including Frontier's 700MW off-grid plant (210 Jenbacher reciprocating engines, TCEQ-approved) — with up to 98% criteria-pollutant emissions reduction and hydrogen/RNG optionality.

Against Crusoe's owned energy stack and Aligned's grid-first siting, Vantage buys speed through partnership structures — generation is owned/operated by VoltaGrid or Liberty, keeping Vantage's balance sheet on buildings while still controlling delivery timelines.

Liberty Energy partnership: up to 1GW of power agreements within five years via Liberty Power Innovations — including a 400MW reservation of 2027 generation capacity — owned and operated by LPI for Vantage's North America campuses — A second gigawatt-class generation partner alongside VoltaGrid — Vantage is assembling a dispatchable-power bench the way other developers assemble land banks.

Frontier groundbreaking reported (w.media/DCD): construction underway on the 1.4GW Shackelford County campus for Oracle/OpenAI Stargate; runs off-grid on a 700MW VoltaGrid microgrid — 210 Jenbacher engines, 197 prime + 13 backup (TCEQ filings) — The largest off-grid data-center power plant disclosed to date — Vantage converted its microgrid partnership into a way to simply not wait for ERCOT interconnection.

VoltaGrid partnership: more than 1GW of prime natural-gas microgrid generation to deploy across the North America portfolio — months-scale installation, up to 98% criteria-pollutant reduction, hydrogen/RNG-capable — The first move in what became the Frontier off-grid design — grid constraint converted from a schedule risk into a procurement item.

Vantage Data Centers partnership: >1 GW of VoltaGrid natural-gas microgrids as primary power across Vantage's North America portfolio — The deal that announced the oilfield-to-AIDC pivot had worked — prime power, not just bridge.

evid.text: For the relationship web: it is FEOC-clean by construction (Austrian engines, Swiss electricals, Texas manufacturing), its growth shrinks the addressable BESS layer on the fastest-growing off-grid segment, and where batteries did attach at its sites (xAI Colossus, where VoltaGrid's 35 MW mobile fleet bridged the 122-day bring-up), the buyer precedent was Tesla Megapack.

(Moderate confidence) We assess the residual battery surfaces at VoltaGrid as real but closed to Hithium: the legacy mobile fleet carries undisclosed BESS on its switchgear bus (a small, incumbent-held socket), and bridge-power sites have paired with Tesla Megapacks (xAI precedent) — a §154-named supplier has no visible path into either, and VoltaGrid's FEOC-clean-by-construction stack is part of its customer pitch even if never stated as such.
